title: Elastic Fidelity Gate: playbook for admission heuristics, banded queues, and graceful truncation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: During transient overloads and regional failover events we need an automated, observable mechanism to keep latencies within SLOs while preserving as much end-user quality as possible. The Elastic Fidelity Gate (EFG) is a combined admission + queueing + graceful-degradation system that enforces token- and latency-aware budgets per tenant and route, admits requests into banded priority lanes, and applies automated fidelity reductions (response truncation, cheap-fallback models, compressed format) when needed. This ticket captures the design, acceptance criteria, implementation plan, test matrix, rollout strategy, monitoring, and operator playbook.
motivation: We have frequent short high-percentile latency spikes during backups, multi-region failovers, and model cold-starts. Current blunt shedding (global rate limits, region-wide capacity limits) causes disproportionate customer impact. EFG aims to achieve SLOs more gracefully by making degradation predictable, tier-aware, and reversible.
goals: 1) Keep p99 generation latency below service SLO during overload in 90% of incidents by gracefully degrading quality rather than failing requests. 2) Ensure high-value customers see prioritized admission with minimal quality loss. 3) Provide operators clear controls and an automated rollback path. 4) Expose SLI/quality trade-offs in Console for post-incident analysis.
non_goals: This ticket does not implement long-term model compression or new quantization kernels. It does not change billing semantics (we continue to bill by tokens even for truncated responses).
design_summary: EFG components: 1) Admission estimator: fast in-memory predictor that approximates request cost (tokens, beam-size, expected decode length) using request metadata and historical token distributions. 2) Banded priority lanes: three lanes (critical, standard, background) with per-lane reservoirs (token credits and concurrency slots). 3) Elastic fidelity actions: (A) prefix-truncation (limit max generated tokens), (B) fallback to distilled/cheap model, (C) compressed response (short form / structured summary), (D) early-stop heuristic (stop generation when incremental log-prob sum drops below threshold). 4) Soft-accept: admitted requests can be flagged as 'degradable' and may be post-processed with fidelity actions if queueing or runtime indicators cross thresholds. 5) Predictive preemption: when admission estimator forecasts breach of latency SLO, lower-priority requests are probabilistically rejected or immediately returned with best-effort compressed responses.
data_model_and_state: Per-tenant state: token_credit (rolling window), last_admit_ts, rolling_avg_req_cost, priority_tag. Global state: per-region capacity estimate, lane utilization metrics. State kept in shard-local in-memory stores with periodic persistence to redis for recovery. Reservoir counters use atomic increment/decrement.
admission_policy: - Request classification: determine priority by token, route, and tenant SLA. - Cost estimate: fast lookup based on model, prompt length, prompt-template category. - Admission check: pass if lane credits >= estimated_cost and lane concurrency < slot_limit. - Probabilistic degrade: if lane credits are low, admit with degrade flag at rate proportional to deficit.
fidelity_profiles: Predefined profiles (high-fidelity, balanced, economy) per route and tenant. Profiles list ordered actions: e.g., high-fidelity=['no_truncation','no_fallback'], balanced=['prefix_truncation:0.8','fallback-distilled:0.2'], economy=['prefix_truncation:0.5','fallback-distilled:1.0','compressed:1.0']. Profiles editable in Console and linked to billing tiers.
metrics_and_alerting: Primary SLIs: p99 generation latency, p95 end-to-end latency, error rate (5xx + rejected_by_gate), quality-regression score (eval prompts pass rate). Secondary: lane token_utilization, reservoir_deficit_events, degrade_rate_by_tenant. Alerts: page on p99>target for >3m OR sudden degrade_rate spike >5x baseline. Console dashboard must show per-tenant tradeoff curve: latency vs quality.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit/integration tests for estimator, reservoir accounting, and fidelity actions. 2) Synthetic load test: under 2x baseline load with 20% model cold starts, p99 latency stays within SLO for 90% of runs and degrade_rate <= configured target. 3) Canary: gradual rollout to <=5% traffic with auto-rollback on QoQ quality drop >3%. 4) Operators can manually toggle fidelity_profiles and lane capacities in Console without restart.
testing_plan: Test types: - Unit: estimator math, atomic counters, degrade action correctness. - Integration: local runtime with 3 lanes, simulate token-heavy requests and validate admission decisions and token accounting. - Chaos: region outage simulation with traffic shift to failover region and observe preemption behavior. - Load: k6 script replicating production request mix; assert SLIs. - Eval: run golden prompt set before/after with baseline to measure quality delta. - A/B: compare user-visible quality metrics for canary vs control.
implementation_notes: - Implement estimator as pluggable service inside request router with <500us budget. - Reservoir counters use redis for cross-shard topology but keep hot counters local for performance; periodic reconciliation. - Fidelity actions implemented as middleware transformers so they can be chained. - Integrate with rollout service for canary toggles and with circuit-breaker module to respect global failover actions. - Telemetry: embed decision metadata (est_cost, lane, degrade_flags) into trace/span to enable postmortem analysis.
runbook_and_operator_playbook: Incidents: - Symptom: p99 spikes or surge in conserve_mode_degrades. Actions: 1) view Console lane utilization and reservoir deficits. 2) If deficits localized to region: enable extra capacity (burst pool) or promote dedicated pool. 3) If deficits global: increase truncation aggressiveness via 'economy' profile throttle or raise admission thresholds. 4) If quality regressions observed post-change: rollback to previous profiles via rollout service. Escalation: after 15m with persistent p99>target, page on-call infra. Recovery verification: verify p99 improvement and check quality-regression metric on sample eval set. Post-incident: run the forensic job that replays traces with different fidelity actions to tune thresholds.
rollback_conditions_and_safeguards: Auto-rollback if: quality_regression_score drops >5 percentage points over 5m OR customer_error_rate increases >3x. All fidelity changes are applied via rollout with canary and automatic rollback hooks. Critical customers can opt-out via tenant flags (will reduce their availability under extreme overload).
dashboard_and_console_exposure: Console widgets: lane heatmap, per-tenant credit balance, degrade_rate heatmap, SLO impact estimate slider (simulate more/less aggressive truncation). Expose 'why rejected' reason in API response for debugging (short code, e.g., EFG:DEBT).
security_considerations: No PII stored in estimator. Rate-limiting metadata sanitized. Tenant opt-out controls gated by RBAC. Changes to fidelity profiles audited in audit log. Require security review only if we add new data stores (currently false).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind feature-flag. 2) Unit/integration tests + bench. 3) Internal dogfood in staging with synthetic multi-region failure tests. 4) Canary 1% traffic for 24h with tight monitoring. 5) Ramp to 5% for 48h. 6) Ramp to 25% with ops watch. 7) Full rollout if metrics stable. Each step uses the rollout service with automatic rollback triggers.
open_questions: 1) What should be the default per-tenant token_credit replenishment rate for new tenants? 2) Do we allow billing exemptions for truncated responses (legal impact)? 3) How aggressive should fallback-to-distilled be for chat endpoints where context is important?
next_steps: 1) Spike: implement estimator prototype and benchmark CPU/latency overhead (Owner: Marco). 2) Design review with PM and Design for default profile UX (Owner: Aisha). 3) Implement reservoir persistence shim (Owner: Priya). 4) Create canary dashboard panels and alert rules (Owner: SRE).
